cur:objects-bologna-whalebone-christ-ent.summary: Christ sits on a high-backed throne with a bolster cushion, his feet on a footstool, raising his right hand in blessing and holding a book on his knee. Plant scrolls fill the background on either side of the throne. Carved not from elephant ivory but from whale bone, the plaque shows how the image of Christ in majesty was reproduced in more modest materials.
facts: Whale bone and walrus ivory were used as substitutes when elephant ivory was scarce, particularly in the West in the 10th and 11th centuries (type).
cur:objects-bologna-whalebone-christ-ent.notes: Place of production is uncertain; the museum caption gives only 'mid-10th century, whale bone'.

wga:zearly/2/2paintin/5oberze5.summary: Two linked miracles unfold in one long panel: at the left Christ turns to the woman who has touched the hem of his garment, and then, with his disciples and Jairus, moves toward the house at the right, where the dead girl lies on her bed. The Latin inscriptions beneath echo the gospel words, praising the woman's faith and recording Christ's command to the girl to rise. Painted on the south wall of St. Georg, the scene belongs to the cycle's culminating sequence of raisings from the dead.
facts: German Wikipedia counts this as the seventh scene of the cycle, the Raising of Jairus's Daughter, one of two scenes in which Christ appears twice.
It has been suggested that the north-wall miracles were chosen for their connection with water (the lake side), and the south-wall raisings from the dead for the side facing the presumed cemetery.
A slender tower at the left edge reappears, slightly shortened, in the Stilling of the Storm scene, linking the paintings visually.
wga:zearly/2/2paintin/5oberze5.notes: WGA titles this only by the first episode; the panel also shows the raising of Jairus's daughter (inscription includes 'surge puella'). Christ appears twice, as German Wikipedia notes for this scene. Dating disputed as for the rest of the cycle.
